results.title: Exploring the Nile River: A Journey Through History and Culture - Delfin Tours
results.content:
The Nile River is considered the world’s longest river, covering over 6650 kilometres (4,130 miles), flowing from its source at Lake Victoria in Uganda all the way to the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt. It flows through 11 countries in Northeastern Africa, where it has sustained human civilization over the years. The river contains two main branches, the White Nile and the Blue Nile, which merge at Khartoum, Sudan, before flowing north to the sea. [...] The Nile River is the longest river in the world, flowing over 6650 km through 11 countries in the heart of Africa. Over the years, it has sustained hundreds of millions of people, shaped cultures, and inspired civilization. Today, it draws travelers who wants to experience something more than a normal holiday, and seek to cruise past ancient temples at sunset, explore pharaonic tombs untouched for millennia, or stand at the precise point where two mighty rivers become one.  This guide covers [...] The Nile River is about 6,650 kilometers (4,130 miles) long, making it the world’s longest river. This measurement runs from the Kagera River’s source in Rwanda to the river’s mouth at the Mediterranean Sea. The Nile’s length has been confirmed using satellite technology and GPS measurements, resolving the longstanding debate with the Amazon River over which is longer.

results.content:
Nile River, the longest river in the world, called the father of African rivers. It rises south of the Equator and flows northward through northeastern Africa to drain into the Mediterranean Sea. It has a length of about 4,132 miles (6,650 kilometres) and drains an area estimated at 1,293,000 square miles (3,349,000 square kilometres). Its basin includes parts of Tanzania, Burundi, Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Sudan, and the cultivated part [...] ### How long is the Nile River?

The Nile River is approximately 4,100 miles long and was historically thought to be the longest river in the world. There is plenty of debate surrounding this, however, for many believe the Amazon River in South America might be longer. According to the United States Geological Survey, the Nile is about 100 miles longer than the Amazon. [...] The Nile is formed by three principal streams: the Blue Nile (Arabic: Al-Baḥr Al-Azraq; Amharic: Abay) and the Atbara (Arabic: Nahr ʿAṭbarah), which flow from the highlands of Ethiopia, and the White Nile (Arabic: Al-Baḥr Al-Abyad), the headstreams of which flow into Lakes Victoria and Albert.

results.title: Journey of the Nile | The Longest River in the World | Britannica
results.content: We are following the course of the Nile, the longest river in the world. For 6,600 kilometers it snakes its way through a wild and mysterious continent of thick jungle, wide open plains and vast deserts, until it finally reaches its goal, the expansive Nile Delta on the Mediterranean coast. [...] The Nile proceeds from Lake Victoria through Uganda and on to Sudan. This is where the White Nile meets the much shorter Blue Nile, which flows north from the mountains of Ethiopia and over mighty waterfalls of its own. As the Nile crosses the border between Sudan and Egypt, its environment changes considerably. Now it is passing through the Sahara. The banks of the Nile are a unique and thriving habitat for wildlife right in the middle of the desert. The river flows through the desert for over [...] The Nile's long journey begins in the heart of Africa. It flows down from the mountains of Rwanda and Burundi to join Lake Victoria. The place where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria in Uganda is known as the source of the Nile. This very special place is said to possess a unique force. This is where the Nile plunges down the Bujagali Falls. The natives believe that these falls have a mighty power - the power to destroy, but also to nourish and to heal.
